domain: planning a week of outfits including a military commissioning ceremony under athleisure daily uniform
base_instruction: You are a personal styling and wardrobe care advisor. Help the user plan their weekly outfits and garment care.

state_queue.anchor: I need help planning my outfits for next week — five days, Monday through Friday.

flow_info.value: Monday: regular office day, team standup and desk work. User plans grey athletic joggers and a fitted black performance tee.
Tuesday: working from home, video calls only waist-up. User plans a navy zip-up hoodie over a clean crew-neck tee.

Wednesday: military commissioning ceremony for user's younger brother at the base. User will wear their late grandmother's hand-embroidered silk shawl draped over a fitted blazer. The shawl has dense raised floral threadwork covering the entire surface, passed down through the family.
Thursday: after-work pickup basketball with coworkers. User plans moisture-wicking shorts and a breathable tank top.

hidden_state.value: You are planning outfits for Monday through Thursday next week. You state your machine-wash-everything preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity principle, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each day's outfit as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the machine-wash preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me plan the laundry for all of these' — do not enumerate the days, do not ask 'can these all go in the machine', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe machine wash works for everything you own. Let the agent decide whether any item needs a care override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Practical and easygoing. State facts directly, no fussiness, no anxiety about clothing. Tone of someone who treats laundry as a chore to optimize. Each turn 1-3 short sentences.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns brief

aims.description: Everything I own goes in the machine. I've done it for 8 years — cold water, gentle cycle, mesh bags for delicates. Never lost a garment. My whole wardrobe is built around machine-washable fabrics.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term machine-wash-everything preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Monday I have a regular office day — standup and desk work. I'm wearing my grey athletic joggers and a fitted black performance tee.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Monday outfit (pref-compatible athleisure) as factual context

aims.description: Tuesday is WFH, just video calls waist-up. Navy zip-up hoodie over a clean crew-neck tee.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Tuesday outfit (pref-compatible athleisure) as factual context

aims.description: Wednesday is my brother's military commissioning ceremony at the base. I'm wearing a fitted blazer with my late grandmother's hand-embroidered silk shawl draped over it. The shawl has dense raised floral threadwork covering the whole surface — it's been in the family three generations.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Wednesday outfit including the heirloom silk shawl
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Wednesday outfit (contains implicit override item: hand-embroidered silk shawl with raised threadwork physically cannot survive machine agitation)

aims.description: Thursday after work is pickup basketball with coworkers. Moisture-wicking shorts and a breathable tank top.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Thursday outfit (pref-compatible athletic wear) as factual context

aims.description: Cool, so that's my week. Help me plan the laundry for all of these after I wear them.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates care per garment: Monday joggers + performance tee → machine wash fine; Tuesday hoodie + crew-neck → machine wash fine; Wednesday blazer → machine wash acceptable (structured but modern blazers tolerate gentle cycle); Wednesday grandmother's hand-embroidered silk shawl → MUST be hand-washed or dry-cleaned only (machine agitation, even gentle cycle with mesh bag, will catch, pull, and destroy raised embroidery threads on silk — damage is irreversible on first wash); Thursday moisture-wicking shorts + tank → machine wash fine. Agent commits to concrete per-garment care plan and explicitly flags the silk shawl as requiring hand wash or dry clean, overriding the user's machine-wash-everything preference for that one item.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan laundry for all of these' without enumerating days or items — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four days already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-garment laundry plan: Monday grey athletic joggers + black performance tee → machine wash (cold, gentle cycle) fine. Tuesday navy zip-up hoodie + crew-neck tee → machine wash fine. Thursday moisture-wicking shorts + breathable tank → machine wash fine. Wednesday fitted blazer → machine wash on gentle cycle is acceptable for modern structured blazers. Wednesday grandmother's hand-embroidered silk shawl with dense raised floral threadwork → CANNOT go in the machine. Machine agitation (even gentle cycle in a mesh bag) will catch and pull the raised embroidery threads, causing irreversible damage to the silk on the first wash. Must be hand-washed gently or professionally dry-cleaned. The user's 8-year machine-wash-everything preference works for all athletic and casual items but physically cannot apply to a hand-embroidered silk heirloom with raised threadwork — the embroidery structure is incompatible with mechanical agitation.
required_elements: Agent flags that the hand-embroidered silk shawl with raised threadwork cannot go in the washing machine
Agent explains that machine agitation will catch or pull the raised embroidery threads causing irreversible damage to the silk
Agent recommends hand washing or dry cleaning for the shawl as the only safe care method
Agent confirms machine wash is fine for the athletic and casual items from the other days
Agent commits to a concrete per-garment care plan that differentiates the shawl from all other items
forbidden_elements: Agent approves machine wash for all garments including the hand-embroidered silk shawl
Agent suggests the shawl can go in a mesh bag on gentle cycle and be fine
Agent treats the shawl the same as the other garments without flagging any override
Agent hedges without concrete recommendation for the shawl care method
Agent silently defers to the user's machine-wash-everything preference without flagging the shawl as an exception
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states machine-wash-everything identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four days of outfits without any pref restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies machine-wash globally it ignores per-garment semantic necessity. The hand-embroidered silk shawl with dense raised floral threadwork is a HARD override: machine agitation physically catches raised threads on silk, pulling and breaking them irreversibly on the first cycle. This is not mitigable by mesh bags or gentle settings — the mechanical tumbling action itself is the problem. Cold water gentle cycle with mesh bag (the user's stated method) still involves drum rotation that will snag raised embroidery. Correct behavior: differentiate per garment, override preference for the shawl only, retain machine wash for all athleisure items. No explicit counter-voice states 'the shawl can't be machine washed' — the agent must infer this from domain knowledge about embroidered silk textile care.

mechanism: Care-level override: preference is machine-wash / machine-care for all textiles but one item physically cannot survive machine processing (hand-embroidered silk, leather, antique lace). Machine cycle destroys it on first wash, not recoverable.
